intro: Excerpts copied from the live Lottery Wiz source (C:\Lottery Wiz). Each shows the real code behind a capability and explains how it powers that feature. The math lives in two pure-Python engines (engine_py.py for Fantasy 5, lottery_general.py for any game) shared by the FastAPI server, the browser, and the MCP server. Throughout, covering designs restructure coverage but never change the odds.

snippets.title: Fantasy 5 greedy covering wheel
snippets.code:
def gen_wheel(pool, t=3, seed=1):
    pool = sorted(pool); v = len(pool)
    if v < PICK:
        return []
    tsubs_needed = set(combinations(pool, t))
    need = len(tsubs_needed)
    covered = set(); rng = random.Random(seed); tickets = []; guard = 0
    while len(covered) < need and guard < 6000:
        guard += 1
        best = None; best_gain = -1
        tries = min(400, max(120, v * 8))
        for _ in range(tries):
            cand = _combo(pool, rng)
            gain = sum(1 for c in combinations(cand, t) if c not in covered)
            if gain > best_gain:
                best_gain = gain; best = cand
                if gain == C(PICK, t): break
        if not best or best_gain <= 0: break
        for c in combinations(best, t): covered.add(c)
        tickets.append(best)
    return tickets
snippets.explanation: The heart of the tool. It enumerates every t-subset of your pool that must be covered, then greedily adds the 5-number ticket that covers the most still-uncovered t-subsets, repeating until all are covered. That yields the combinatorial guarantee: if at least t of your pool numbers are drawn, at least one ticket shows a t-match. It restructures coverage of the combination space; it does not change the per-ticket odds.

snippets.title: Generalized wheel for any N/k/t
snippets.explanation: The same covering-design idea generalized to any game: any ticket size k, any guarantee t, any pool. When the number of candidate k-subsets is small enough it enumerates them all for an optimal-ish cover; otherwise it samples. This single function backs Powerball, Mega Millions, EuroMillions, Mega-Sena and every other Universal game — the bonus ball is handled separately because it is an independent draw and cannot be wheeled.

snippets.title: The 6-step curated funnel
snippets.explanation: The transparent funnel: from the C(pool,5) space, drop combinations that already occurred in history, drop statistical 'edge' shapes, then rank survivors by profile fit. Every count (in_pool, removed_past, removed_edges, survivors, selected) is returned so the UI can show the funnel. It refuses pools that explode past 200k combinations — that ceiling enforces the research's core 'reduced universe' principle.

snippets.title: Coverage-aware greedy selection
snippets.feature: Maximise pair/triple coverage while keeping profile high
snippets.explanation: After scoring, the set is built greedily from the top-profile window, but each pick is penalised (lam) for reusing number-pairs already covered by chosen tickets. This balances two goals at once: keep the high-profile shapes AND spread coverage across the pool, so the final set's pair/triple coverage is high rather than clustering on the same favourite pairs.

snippets.title: What counts as an 'edge' to drop
snippets.code:
def is_edge(t):
    """An 'edge' = a statistically extreme combination the research advises against."""
    a = sorted(t)
    if all(a[i + 1] - a[i] == 1 for i in range(4)):          # all consecutive
        return True
    odd = sum(1 for x in a if x % 2)
    if odd in (0, 5):                                        # all odd / all even
        return True
    low = sum(1 for x in a if x <= LOW_MAX)
    if low in (0, 5):                                        # all low / all high
        return True
    d = a[1] - a[0]
    if d > 0 and all(a[i + 1] - a[i] == d for i in range(4)):  # arithmetic progression
        return True
    if a[-1] - a[0] <= 6:                                    # tight cluster (range <= 6)
        return True
    if sum(a) < 60 or sum(a) > 150:                          # extreme sum
        return True
    return False
snippets.explanation: The edge filter encodes the research's advice against shapes that, while equally likely, almost never reflect real draws and waste coverage: all-consecutive, all-odd/even, all-low/high, arithmetic progressions, tight range<=6 clusters, and extreme sums. Dropping them concentrates the curated set on draw-realistic shapes — honestly framed as scoring SHAPE, not likelihood.

snippets.title: Transparent profile score
snippets.code:
a = sorted(t); f = ticket_features(t)
sum_sc = math.exp(-((f["sum"] - 107) / 22.0) ** 2)        # peak at the ~107 hotzone centre
oe_sc = 1.0 if f["odd"] in (2, 3) else (0.5 if f["odd"] in (1, 4) else 0.1)
lh_sc = 1.0 if f["low"] in (2, 3) else (0.5 if f["low"] in (1, 4) else 0.1)
consec_sc = 1.0 if f["consec"] == 0 else (0.5 if f["consec"] == 1 else 0.1)
spread_sc = min(1.0, (a[-1] - a[0]) / 30.0)               # reward spread, discourage clustering
score = 0.34 * sum_sc + 0.18 * oe_sc + 0.18 * lh_sc + 0.15 * consec_sc + 0.08 * spread_sc + 0.07 * nov_sc
snippets.explanation: Each candidate gets a 0–1 fit to the documented Fantasy 5 profile: a gaussian peak at the ~107 sum hotzone, a 2-3/3-2 odd-even and low-high balance, zero consecutive numbers, good spread, and novelty versus recent draws. The weights are explicit and the function returns its per-component breakdown, so the ranking is fully auditable — not a black box.

snippets.title: Hypergeometric win-tier probability
snippets.explanation: The honest baseline. p_exactly is the hypergeometric probability of exactly k of your 5 numbers matching the 5 drawn; p_any_atleast lifts it to 'at least one of T independent tickets gets >=k'. These are the true odds and they do NOT change with any strategy — the app shows them precisely so a covering wheel is never mistaken for an edge.

snippets.title: Best-ticket backtest over history
snippets.feature: Backtest a set against real draws
snippets.explanation: For every historical draw it records the BEST single-ticket match in the set, bucketed 0–5. The ge3/ge4 rates are exactly how the documented research sets are validated (e.g. S1-01 reproducing >=3=1926, >=4=64, jackpots=2). It answers 'how often would this set have done something' across thousands of real draws.

snippets.title: Bitmask payout replay
snippets.code:
tmasks = [_mask(t) for t in tickets]
dmasks = [_mask(d) for d in draws]
outlay = len(tmasks) * cost
for dm in dmasks:
    draw_payout = 0.0
    for tm in tmasks:
        m = (tm & dm).bit_count()
        tiers[m] += 1
        draw_payout += pay_tier[m]
    recovered += draw_payout
    spend += outlay
    equity.append(round(recovered - spend, 2))
    if draw_payout > best_win:
        best_win = draw_payout
    if draw_payout < outlay:
        cur_streak += 1; worst_streak = max(worst_streak, cur_streak)
    else:
        cur_streak = 0
snippets.explanation: The signature feature. Each ticket and each draw is an integer bitmask, so the match count is one popcount (bit_count) — making thousands of draws cheap. It accumulates real spend vs recovered with full payout math, builds an equity curve, and tracks the best single-draw win and the worst losing streak. The output is the blunt financial reality of actually playing this set across history.

snippets.title: Exact random-quick-pick control
snippets.feature: Compare your set against pure luck
snippets.code:
probs = [p_exactly(m) for m in range(6)]
n_trials = n_tickets_per_draw * n_draws
spend_total = n_tickets_per_draw * cost * n_draws
try:
    import numpy as np
    rs = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    counts = rs.multinomial(n_trials, probs, size=runs)        # runs x 6
    recovered = counts @ np.array(pay_tier)
    nets = sorted((recovered - spend_total).tolist())
    return nets
snippets.explanation: Because a uniformly-random ticket's match count against ANY fixed draw has the same hypergeometric distribution by symmetry, every (ticket, draw) payout is i.i.d. — so a whole random-quick-pick run is ONE multinomial draw over n_tickets*n_draws trials. numpy makes thousands of control runs exact and microsecond-fast (with a pure-Python fallback). percentile_of then reports where your strategy lands versus luck — usually the honest 'didn't beat random'.

snippets.title: Hypergeometric prize tiers, k != draw size
snippets.feature: Exact odds for any lottery + bonus ball
snippets.explanation: The generalized odds engine. It handles games where the ticket size k differs from the draw size D (Lotomania picks 50 of 100 but only 20 are drawn; Timemania picks 10, draws 7) via the full hypergeometric, and multiplies in the independent bonus pool C(Bn,b). Verified exact against published odds (Powerball 1/292,201,338, EuroMillions 1/139,838,160, 6/49 1/13,983,816).

snippets.title: Super Sete Poisson-binomial odds
snippets.code:
probs = [max(0, min(10, int(c))) / 10.0 for c in counts]
pmf = [1.0]  # DP over columns
for p in probs:
    nxt = [0.0] * (len(pmf) + 1)
    for j, val in enumerate(pmf):
        nxt[j]     += val * (1 - p)   # column missed
        nxt[j + 1] += val * p         # column hit
    pmf = nxt
return pmf
snippets.explanation: Super Sete is 7 independent columns; in each you mark 1–3 of the digits 0–9, so the per-column hit probability is marks_i/10. The number of matched columns is a Poisson-binomial, computed exactly by this DP convolution. With one mark per column it reduces to the published 7/7 = 1 in 10,000,000, 6 = 1 in 158,730, etc. — verified against Caixa's table.

snippets.title: US official feed (data.ny.gov)
snippets.code:
url = f"https://data.ny.gov/resource/{resource}.json?$order=draw_date%20DESC&$limit={limit}"
for r in json.loads(_get(url)):
    date = (r.get("draw_date") or "")[:10]
    toks = [int(x) for x in (r.get("winning_numbers") or "").split()]
    if mode == "powerball":            # winning_numbers = 5 main + powerball (6 tokens)
        out.append({"date": date, "n": sorted(toks[:5]), "b": [toks[5]]})
    elif mode == "megamillions":       # 5 main + separate mega_ball
        out.append({"date": date, "n": sorted(toks[:5]), "b": [int(r.get("mega_ball", 0))]})
    elif mode == "cash4life":          # 5 main + separate cash_ball
        out.append({"date": date, "n": sorted(toks[:5]), "b": [int(r.get("cash_ball", 0))]})
snippets.explanation: One of several fetchers behind 'Get latest results'. It reads the official NY State Socrata API, handling each game's quirk: Powerball packs the bonus as the 6th token of winning_numbers, while Mega Millions and Cash4Life carry it in a separate field. Each draw normalises to {date, n, b} and the server merges it into data/draws/<id>.json, deduping by date. Games with no reliable free source say so honestly and fall back to CSV import.

snippets.title: Caixa gap-close walk-back
snippets.code:
base = f"https://servicebus2.caixa.gov.br/portaldeloterias/api/{slug}"
cur = json.loads(_get(base)); pulled = 0
while cur and pulled <= max_pull:
    date = _br_date(cur.get("dataApuracao"))
    dz = cur.get("listaDezenas") or cur.get("dezenasSorteadasOrdemSorteio") or []
    nums = sorted(int(x) for x in dz)
    if date and nums:
        rec = {"date": date, "n": nums}
        if game_id == "diadesorte":
            m = PT_MONTH.get((cur.get("nomeTimeCoracaoMesSorte") or "").strip().lower())
            if m: rec["b"] = [m]
        out.append(rec)
    if last_date and date and date <= last_date: break
    prev = cur.get("numeroConcursoAnterior") or ((cur.get("numero") or 0) - 1)
    cur = json.loads(_get(f"{base}/{prev}")); pulled += 1
snippets.explanation: The Brazilian fetcher walks backward from the latest Caixa contest, contest by contest, until it reaches the last date already stored — closing any gap rather than re-pulling everything. It also parses each game's special bonus: Dia de Sorte's lucky-month name maps to 1–12, and +Milionaria's trevos (clovers) become the bonus pool. Caixa is the official source, so these eight games update reliably.

snippets.title: Constant-time owner-key check
snippets.feature: Owner lock on preset game definitions
snippets.explanation: Public visitors can use every game and build their own lotteries, but the official preset DEFINITIONS are read-only. The owner key is read from an env var, else a gitignored .owner_key file, else auto-generated on first boot so a key always exists. Validation uses hmac.compare_digest (constant-time, no timing leak) and the endpoint never returns the key — only a boolean.

snippets.title: AI drives the app via an action block
snippets.feature: Ask Wiz builds the same set the buttons do
snippets.explanation: When Wiz is asked to build something it replies with one short sentence then a fenced 'lotterywiz' action block. The dock parses it and applyAiActions executes it by driving the REAL controls — switching the game, setting the pool/method/size, then calling the same generate() the buttons call. The AI never invents numbers; its result is byte-identical to a manual build, which is what makes the assistant trustworthy.

snippets.title: Streaming chat with per-app prompts
snippets.explanation: Each of the four apps gets its own system prompt — and every prompt insists the AI be honest that the numbers are equiprobable and unpredictable. The live app state (current game N/k, draws loaded) is injected as JSON so Wiz reasons about the actual configuration. /api/chat then streams tokens as Server-Sent Events from local Ollama by default (or a cloud model if a key exists).

snippets.title: Brutal Ledger as an MCP tool
snippets.feature: Drive Lottery Wiz from Claude Desktop (no paid API)
snippets.explanation: One of 11 FastMCP tools. Because it imports engine_py directly, Claude Desktop runs the exact same ledger + random-control math as the web app — over the user's subscription with no per-token billing. It returns the full honest verdict (spend, recovered, net, ROI, tiers, percentile vs random) in one call, dropping the long equity curve to stay chat-friendly.
